newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas still presssured late by technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas still presssured late by technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, defying reports of firmer physical prices, remained broadly lower late Thursday in active trade, still undermined by technical selling after an early rally attempt stalled.

By 1400 EDT, June tumbled 9.1 cents to $2.185 per million British thermal units after opening in the $2.28 area. July was 8.5 cents lower at $2.19, while most other deferreds were down one to seven cents.
"We've seen longs getting out today, but I think there's pretty good support in the teens (basis June), and with cash up, we could move up from here," said an East Coast trader.
Technical traders agreed June support was in the $2.15 area, with major buying likely at $2.05. Resistance was seen at $2.30 and then at contract high of $2.43.
While steady injections and heat in the Southwest have helped support the cash this month, most agreed it would take broader cooling loads to break to new highs.
Weather next week in the Southeast was expected to warm to slightly above-normal, while seasonal to slightly-below seasonal temperatures were forecast for the Midwest and Northeast.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained a few cents Thursday to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the $2.03-2.08 area. New York city gate gas also was up slightly in the high-$2.40s.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will continue to cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
NYMEX said 25,397 contracts traded at 1230 EDT. Hub open interest on May 14 rose 1,018 contracts to 206,633.
On KCBT, June was still down by five cents at $2.05, while deferreds were steady to 5.5 cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 4.1 cents to 13.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
